question: Which table does record_outcome actually write against?
root_cause: record_outcome writes against NEITHER prediction ledger — and there are TWO distinct record_outcome tool surfaces targeting two DIFFERENT tables, neither of which is mimamsa_predictions. (1) The MCP direct tool named 'record_outcome' (platform-mcp/src/tools/mimamsa_outcome.ts) calls the sidecar /api/compute/mimamsa/record_outcome (python-sidecar/brahmagyan/mimamsa/outcome.py), which UPDATEs phala_anchors (prediction_state, outcome_note, outcome_recorded_at) then calls update_calibration() -> mimamsa_calibration. (2) The P1 alias 'mimamsa_outcome_record' calls callPlatformPrim('record_outcome') -> /api/mcp/writes/record_outcome -> ppl_writer.recordOutcome() which UPDATEs mcp_predictions (same-row outcome cols). So: 'record_outcome' the tool resolves outcomes against phala_anchors+mimamsa_calibration; 'mimamsa_outcome_record' resolves against mcp_predictions; mimamsa_predictions' own lifecycle is transitioned only by build-time mi_abhilekha.py, never by any record_outcome. ADDITIONAL DEFECT: the sidecar outcome.py SELECTs/UPDATEs phala_anchors columns that do NOT exist in the live schema — it references id, confidence, prediction_state, outcome_note, outcome_recorded_at, updated_at, but live phala_anchors has anchor_id, confidence_low/high, posterior, computed_at and none of those outcome columns. The sidecar record_outcome would fail at runtime against live phala_anchors (schema drift, separate from OT-11 but bears on 'which table record_outcome writes').

question: Cost both options — (A) merge the ledgers into one, (B) keep both/three and document the split. Does either table alone satisfy §14 without a schema change?
root_cause: BOTH OPTIONS COSTED, NO CHOICE MADE (PC-8). OPTION A (merge into one canonical ledger): schema work — unify incompatible types (chart_id text->uuid backfill+validate; horizon text->daterange parse; confidence text-enum->numeric mapping so Brier can score chat-captured rows); ADD the §14.3 columns NEITHER has (message_part_id FK, created_from_channel, the 8-state lifecycle enum); reconcile two disjoint id namespaces (PH-4-1.* vs PPL.*); and fold in brahma_prospective_ledger (5 rows) + reconcile phala_anchors as record_outcome's real target for a truly single ledger. Code rewrites: mi_bhavisya/mi_abhilekha/mi_pramana, mimamsa_calibration.prediction_id linkage, query_predictions.ts, ppl_writer.ts, calibration_producer.ts, BOTH record_outcome surfaces, assetClearSpec count_sql. Migration RISK concentrated on mimamsa_predictions — the only populated+referenced ledger (384 rows) and the single thing L5 STRUCTURAL-mode calibration depends on; mcp_predictions data-migration is trivial (0 rows) but its writer must be repointed. What breaks if done wrong: the mimamsa_calibration FK, the mi_pramana build step, the cockpit count, the §7.4 NO-LEAKAGE role that must name one table. OPTION B (keep + document): no schema/migration risk; ongoing cost is permanent reader confusion — a caller invoking 'record_outcome' hits phala_anchors+mimamsa_calibration while 'mimamsa_outcome_record' hits mcp_predictions and neither hits mimamsa_predictions; §7.4 role_ledger_write still cannot name one physical table. Documentation needed: a ledger-map declaring authority (mimamsa_predictions=build-time deterministic analytical predictions, referenced by calibration; mcp_predictions=chat-side interim PPL relay, 0 rows, TODO-migrate; brahma_prospective_ledger=D-4a §11 explicit-filing prospective ledger; phala_anchors=L4 anchors record_outcome resolves against) PLUS record_outcome tool disambiguation. Is the split semantically justified? PARTIALLY-YES as a fact: build-time analytical predictions vs conversationally-surfaced live predictions IS a principled provenance distinction the architecture's own §14.1 endorses (the conversation surface as the intended outcome-data channel); but the AS-BUILT three-table state tangles that one clean axis with two-three historical interim scaffolds (mcp_predictions predates §14; brahma_prospective_ledger is a later third attempt), and §14.3's named target table matches none of them. DOES EITHER SATISFY §14 ALONE WITHOUT SCHEMA CHANGE? NO for both — §14.3 mandates message_part_id-FK utterance provenance + created_from_channel + the 8-state lifecycle, which neither has; mimamsa_predictions is closest on the calibration/probabilistic side (numrange confidence, base_rate, calibration FK) but lacks utterance provenance; mcp_predictions is closest on conversational capture (co-located outcomes, caller_context) but its text confidence is Brier-unusable and it lacks window start/end and technique attribution.
